title: Windows runner: process-owner bootstrap log write fails at 261-char path in linked-worktree launcher fixtures (MAX_PATH)
outcome: On Windows, the launcher's process-owner bootstrap logging never fails because of path length. The 'launcher Git path … linked worktree with spaces' tests pass for any source root of reasonable length, rather than depending on a few characters of headroom under MAX_PATH.
acceptance: The root cause is recorded with evidence: scripts/test-process-owner-windows.ps1:5 [IO.File]::AppendAllText(RequestPath+'.bootstrap.jsonl') throws DirectoryNotFoundException when the path is 261 characters. A note states which component is changed: the owner script, the run-path layout, or the fixture depth.

The fix makes bootstrap logging robust to long run paths on Windows: for example, writing via an extended-length path, or keeping owner bootstrap files on the existing short compiler-scratch root. No timeout or assertion is weakened, and the run path is not silently truncated.
A regression test on Windows exercises a source root long enough that the old code's bootstrap path would exceed 260 characters, and passes with the fix.
The standard full gate passes on the landed tree, and a Windows B TermAl full gate on a master tree containing the fix passes fingerprint-tests.
